title: Engineering ATP import in yeast uncovers a synthetic route to extend cellular lifespan
abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction and declining ATP production are common features of aging, yet whether ATP availability itself directly regulates cellular lifespan is unclear. However, the causal relationship between cellular ATP homeostasis and aging has not been established. Here, we developed a synthetic system to manipulate intracellular ATP independently of endogenous energy production by expressing a plasma membrane-targeted nucleotide transporter, NTT1, from the intracellular parasite Encephalitozoon cuniculi in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. NTT1 expression depleted intracellular ATP in the absence of extracellular ATP, whereas ATP supplementation produced robust NTT1-dependent ATP uptake, and increased intracellular ATP abundance. ATP availability strongly influenced replicative lifespan: ATP depletion shortened lifespan, whereas ATP supplementation restored and extended lifespan in NTT1-expressing cells. Unexpectedly, extracellular ATP also extended lifespan

title: Rethinking psychosocial rehabilitation in mental health
abstract:
by Eleonora Prina, Laura Asher, Stefano Barlati, Sudipto Chatterjee, Ioana Alina Cristea, Sandra Ferreira, Charlotte Hanlon, Karli Montague-Cardoso, Parth Sharma, Marianna Purgato, Corrado Barbui

Summary points

Psychosocial rehabilitation is central to recovery-oriented mental health care, yet its uptake remains uneven because of persistent conceptual, methodological, organisational, and implementation barriers. Greater conceptual clarity is needed through stakeholder dialogue to establish a common set of core principles that can be adapted across diverse cultural and health system contexts. Meaningful co-creation with people with lived experience and their families should be embedded throughout the research and implementation cycle, from priority setting and intervention design to evaluation, scale-up, and dissemination. title: Intelligent classification of medically and veterinary important mosquito vectors using self-distillation-enhanced supervised learning
abstract:
by Santhad Chuwongin, Morakot Kaewthamasorn, Tanawat Chaiphongpachara, Sedthapong Laojun, Tawee Saiwichai, Naruchit Soiphet, Siridech Boonsang, Veerayuth Kittichai

Mosquito-borne diseases remain a persistent global public health burden, with effective control strategies depending on the accurate and timely identification of mosquito species and estimation of their population density. The current gold standard, morphological identification via microscopic examination, is limited by inter-observer variability and a scarcity of local taxonomic expertise. While highly accurate, molecular techniques like polymerase chain reaction and DNA barcoding are often impractical for widespread field use due to their cost, procedural complexity, and reliance on specialized equipment and technicians. title: Implementation of mental health screening tools among women refugees and asylum seekers in the United States: A systematic review
abstract:
by Pierre J. Amiel, Shalini Suresh, Abdulaziz Almuhanna, Pratik Chhetri, John Pateña, Joyce Gyamfi, Dorice Vieira, Chukwuemeka Iloegbu, Emmanuel Peprah

Globally, displaced populations face significant mental health challenges, with women refugees and asylum seekers experiencing greater risks of anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder. Despite the widespread use of mental health screening tools such as the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9), the Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD-7), and the Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Checklist (PCL-5), their implementation among refugee women remains underexplored. This systematic review examines the adoption, appropriateness, acceptability, and fidelity of use of mental health screening tools for adult women refugees and asylum seekers in the United States. By identifying and synthesizing evidence on critical gaps, this study aims to inform improvements in mental health screening and care for this vulnerable population. A

title: Life-cycle plasticity enables conditional asexual reproduction in a kelp
abstract:
by Daniel Liesner, Rémy Luthringer, Lineekela Kandjengo, John J. Bolton, Mark D. Rothman, Myriam Valero, Fabian B. Haas, Susana M. Coelho

Many organisms alternate between distinct life stages and can reproduce either sexually or asexually, yet the mechanisms coordinating these developmental and reproductive transitions remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the molecular basis of life stage identity and reproductive mode in the kelp Laminaria pallida, a multicellular organism with a complex life cycle. By combining gene expression analyses with developmental experiments and natural population-level approaches, we characterize the transcriptional signatures associated with developmental state transitions in both sexual and asexual contexts. We show that asexual reproduction is associated with endoreduplication and reduced fitness, while it is retained but rarely expressed in two natural populations. title: The single Cryptosporidium rhoptry sequentially drives invasion and host-parasite interface formation
abstract:
by Allison Cohen, Tim Bergner, Amandine Guérin, Maryse Lebrun, Michael Laue, Christian Klotz, Boris Striepen

The apicomplexan parasite Cryptosporidium is a leading cause of diarrheal disease in young children. Within the intestinal epithelium, Cryptosporidium establishes a unique intracellular niche in the apical brush border of enterocytes. A structurally complex interface between host and parasite acts as a holdfast and enables protein and metabolite transport. How the parasite invades its host cell and builds the interface is poorly understood. Here, we reveal parasite invasion with high temporal and spatial resolution using rigorous molecular markers. We find that sequential discharge of specialized secretory organelles anchors the parasite within the host prior to internalization. title: PhagoCyt enables isolation of Salmonella-containing phagosomes and mapping of host and bacteria remodelling of the intracellular niche
abstract:

Macrophages engulf pathogens into dynamic phagosomes, which many bacteria manipulate for survival. However, isolating pure pathogen-containing phagosomes remains challenging. Here, we developed a novel flow cytometry-based isolation and ultrasensitive proteomics approach to analyse phagosomal and bacterial proteomes from macrophages infected with wild-type (WT) Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium (STM) or a ΔphoP mutant at 30 min and 4 hours post-infection. Our approach provides higher throughput, requires lower cell numbers and quantifies more proteins than previous techniques. title: Vertebrate paired fins are specified by an ancient dorso-ventral patterning system
abstract:
by Rebecca E. Dale, Silke Berger, Sara Alaei, Marcus C. Davis, Frank J. Tulenko, Peter D. Currie

The origin of paired fins was a major event in early vertebrate history that fueled the adaptive radiation of the gnathostome clade. Evidence for the conservation of ancient regulatory systems between paired and median fins supports a model in which appendage-patterning mechanisms first evolved in the midline and were later redeployed to a new embryonic context, the flank. However, while paired fins and limbs are asymmetric along the dorsoventral (DV) axis, the equivalent axis does not exist in median fins, which are symmetric across the midline, raising questions of how DV patterning evolved. title: Association of food consumption patterns with height growth of children and adolescents: A population-based observational study over four decades of food transitions in China
abstract:
by Tianze Li, Jiajia Dang, Yan Li, Wenhua Ling, Leah Li, Cunrui Huang, Yit Siew Chin, Yueqin Zhou, Shiyun Luo, Shan Cai, Peijin Hu, Jun Ma, Min Xia, Yanna Zhu, Yi Song

Background

Height is a key marker of early-life nutrition and health. China’s four-decade food transition provides an opportunity to examine associations between food consumption and child/adolescent height. We aimed to identify food consumption patterns associated with greater height and favorable sustainability profiles and develop a score quantifying food–height associations.

Methods and findings

We conducted an observational study using height data from ~1.7 million Chinese students aged 7–18 years in the Chinese National Survey on Students’ Constitution and Health (1985–2019) and provincial food consumption data from the National Bureau of Statistics (1985–2023). title: Communication-aware dynamic graph learning for V2X misbehavior detection using GAT–BiLSTM and bagged trees
abstract:
by Yuee Zhang, Ping Wang, Xinyu Wang, Xiao Zheng

Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication supports cooperative driving, which also makes the malicious vehicle-state reports influence nearby vehicles. Due to the isolated use of physical state and cross-time communication context, existing methods struggle to detect malicious reports that are physically self-consistent and only reveal inconsistencies at the temporal communication level. Thus, this paper proposes a sequence-level misbehavior detection framework based on graph attention networks (GAT) and bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM). Recorded sender–receiver interactions define a directed communication graph for each one-second window. The GAT can learn the neighboring information contributes to detection. The BiLSTM captures changes across ten consecutive graph snapshots. The resulting representation is fused with physical statistics. Then, a bagged-tree ensemble is introduced to classify it. title: RGDfC-functionalized gold nanoclusters versus the clinical radiosensitizer sodium glycididazole in triple-negative breast cancer radiotherapy
abstract:
by Xiangchao Song, Lingwei Wang, Chunyin Li, Chengbin Qu, Jianyu Xiao

Radiotherapy for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is often limited by intrinsic tumor radioresistance. The clinically approved radiosensitizer sodium glycididazole (CMNa) is restricted by its hypoxia-dependent activity and lack of tumor targeting. Integrin-targeted gold nanoclusters have been extensively investigated as radiosensitizers, yet direct head-to-head comparisons with CMNa are lacking. We synthesized RGDfC-gold nanoclusters (RGDfC-AuNCs) via one-step biomineralization and compared them with CMNa in 4T1 murine TNBC cells and tumor-bearing mice. The nanoclusters showed ultrasmall size, good stability, and exhibited enhanced cellular uptake relative to non-targeted controls. In vitro, radiosensitization performance was assessed by CCK‑8 assays under normoxic and CoCl2‑mimicked pseudo‑hypoxic conditions. title: Proposed approach for diagnosing obesity outperforms old method
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03425-0

A framework for diagnosing obesity that was proposed in 2025 incorporates waist circumference and related measures and distinguishes clinical from preclinical obesity on the basis of obesity-induced organ dysfunction. In an international multi-cohort study of 844,108 adults, this framework outperformed conventional body-mass-index-based criteria in diagnosing obesity and stratifying mortality risk.

title: Brønsted/Lewis acid-catalyzed divergent cascade cyclization of alkoxyallene for the total synthesis of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79505-6

Eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids are biogenetically related yet structurally distinct polycyclic monoterpenoids, whose syntheses have traditionally proceeded separately. Here, the authors report a divergent cascade from a common alkoxyallene precursor, enabling access to both scaffolds through acid controlled tandem pathways and total syntheses of representative alkaloids.

title: Transposons contribute to splice-isoform diversity in the Drosophila brain
abstract: The extraordinary complexity of the brain depends in part on the vast diversity of mRNA isoforms it expresses, often in a cell-type specific manner. In a recent study, we found that intronic transposable elements (TEs) are spliced into neural transcripts and diversify the splice isoform repertoire of neurons and glia (Treiber and Waddell, 2020). A recent paper by Azad et al. revisits these findings using their TIDAL analysis pipeline applied to our published data (Azad et al., 2024). Their analysis did not find any of the splicing reads we reported and although they used RT-PCR to test seven of the 264 TE–gene pairs we had previously reported, they failed to validate TE–gene splicing in any of them. Here, we conduct a quantitative analysis of TE exonisation and show that intronic TE insertions are frequently recruited as alternative exons, with exon usage ranging from rare events to near-complete inclusion in transcripts. title: Endocardial TIE1 synergizes with TIE2 to regulate the atrial internal muscular network assembly
abstract: Atrial cardiomyopathy is characterized by altered atrial structures, yet its underlying genetic basis remains inadequately explored. TIE1 mutations are reported in lymphedema patients, but whether they exhibit cardiac defects alongside lymphatic abnormalities remains unknown. Here, single-cell RNA sequencing showed high Tie1 and Tek expression in atrial endocardial cells. TIE1 deficiency severely disrupted atrial morphogenesis, with only minor ventricular defects. Bulk RNA-seq showed reduced transcripts for endothelial development and cardiac trabeculation in Tie1 mutants. Separate RNA-seq analysis of the atria and ventricles further confirmed these findings, revealing a more pronounced downregulation of trabecular genes, including Tek, in the atria upon Tie1 loss. title: The zoo of the gene networks capable of pattern formation by extracellular signaling
abstract: A fundamental question of developmental biology is pattern formation, or how cells with specific gene expression end up in specific locations in the body to form tissues, organs, and, overall functional anatomy. Pattern formation involves communication through extracellular signals and complex intracellular gene networks integrating these signals to determine cell responses (e.g. further signaling, cell division, cell differentiation, etc.). In this article, we address two questions: (1) Are there any logical or mathematical principles determining which gene network topologies can lead to pattern formation by cell signaling over space in multicellular systems? (2) Can gene network topologies be classified into a small number of classes that entail similar dynamics and pattern transformation capacities?
